ins.title: Winding instructions
ins.subtitle: Frame {d} mm · {pins} pins · threads: {threads} · lines: {lines}
ins.how: Pins are numbered 1 to {pins}, clockwise as seen from the front, with pin 1 at the top (12 o'clock), as on the nail template. Tie each thread to its start pin, then run it from pin to pin in the order printed: along each row from left to right, row after row, down the left column first and then the next. A row holds ten pins; tick its box when it is done. The smaller number after the box is the step the row starts with. The time at the end of a row tells where its first pin is, read as the hour hand of a clock. Wind the threads in the order of this sheet: each one lies on top of those before it.
ins.facts: Start: pin {start} ({startClock}) · End: pin {end} ({endClock}) · Lines: {lines} · Thread: {m} m
ins.howRect: Pins are numbered 1 to {pins}, clockwise as seen from the front, with pin 1 next to the top left corner as the first pin of the top side, as on the nail template: along the top from left to right, down the right side, back along the bottom from right to left, and up the left side. Tie each thread to its start pin, then run it from pin to pin in the order printed: along each row from left to right, row after row, down the left column first and then the next. A row holds ten pins; tick its box when it is done. The smaller number after the box is the step the row starts with. The mark at the end of a row tells where its first pin is: the side it is on and its number along that side, counted the way the pins are numbered, so "right 12" is the twelfth pin down the right side. Wind the threads in the order of this sheet: each one lies on top of those before it.
ins.howInside: There are {inside} more pins inside the picture, numbered on from the frame's, {first} to {last}: in bands of {band} mm from the top, and from left to right in a band. Find them on the nail template (print a second copy to keep beside you) or on the player's map. A hint such as “132 right, 208 down” at the end of a row says that its first pin is inside the picture: 132 mm in from the frame's left edge and 208 mm down from its top. Where a pin number has “~” before it, lead the thread to that pin round the outside of the frame, not across the picture. Some steps run back along a line already wound: that is how the thread gets to its next place, so wind them as they come.
ins.empty: This thread has no lines: skip it.

thread.listHint: The first thread is wound first and lies at the bottom; later threads cover it.
thread.name: Thread name
thread.widthHint: The width the thread appears to have. Fuzz and shadow make thread look wider than its label says.
thread.kind.floss: One strand of embroidery floss (0.40 mm)
calib.title: Measure the thread width from a photo
calib.step1: Wind the thread in parallel lines over the board (or a card of the board's colour), for instance 20 turns spread evenly over 20 mm: the board must show between the threads.
calib.step2: Photograph it from straight above in even light, together with a bare part of the board. No flash, and nothing overexposed.
calib.step3: Choose the photo, drag a frame over a bare part of the board, then one over the threads (inside them, not beyond the outermost thread).
calib.canvas: The calibration photo: drag to mark an area
calib.result: Effective width about {w} mm (the threads cover {percent}% of the area).
calib.need: Mark one area of bare board and one of threads.
calib.problem.same-colour: The thread and the board are too close in colour to measure.
calib.problem.too-light: The two areas are almost equally bright (the threads cover {percent}%): wind the threads closer, or check that the frames are not swapped.
calib.problem.too-dense: The threads are too close (they cover {percent}%); where threads overlap the result is wrong: spread them out and photograph again.
calib.problem.invalid: This can't be measured: mark the areas again.
calib.note: Phone cameras adjust contrast on their own, so this is an estimate; a difference of 0.05 mm does not matter.
order.hint: Tries every winding order on a small version of the picture, then checks the best three at full size.
gamut.title: Can these threads make the picture's colours?
gamut.out: About {percent}% of the picture has colours these threads can't mix; {hue} is missing most.
gamut.fine: These threads can mix every colour of the picture.
gamut.show: Hatch those parts on the picture
auto.title: Let the picture choose the threads
auto.hint: Picks the threads that can best mix the picture's colours, and replaces the current ones. With “Any colour” the result is the ideal: look for the nearest thread you can get.
auto.none: No thread would help: the board's colour is enough.
order.changed: The threads are now in the best order found: {percent}% of the error removed.
order.kept: This order is already the best: {percent}% of the error removed.
frame.spacing: Pins are {gap} mm apart. Near the centre a line can be placed to about {place} mm; fine detail comes from many lines crossing.
frame.spacingRect: The frame is {w} × {h} mm, in the picture's proportions. Pins are {gap} mm apart; the two nearest stand either side of a corner, {nearest} mm apart. Pin 1 is next to the top left corner and the numbers run clockwise.
frame.notSquare: This picture is {w} × {h}, not square: a round frame filled with it shows {percent}% of it at most. A rectangular frame takes the picture's proportions and shows all of it.
frame.insideHint: 0 uses the frame's pins only. Above 0, that many pins are put on the picture's strokes: a line can then run along a stroke instead of crossing the whole frame, which brings a line drawing far closer to the picture. Their places follow this picture, so the board fits this picture only; their heads show in it, and there are about twice the lines.
frame.insidePlaced: {n} placed, at least {gap} mm from one another and from the frame's outline. They are the small dots on the picture.
frame.insideFewer: Only {n} of the {asked} asked for fit this picture, at least {gap} mm from one another and from the frame's outline.
frame.insideDense: The frame's pins stand too close ({gap} mm apart) for a line to leave the frame for a pin inside. Use fewer pins on the frame, or a larger frame.
adjust.rangeHint: Lower darkness for fewer lines. Very light areas will still look grey, because every line crosses the whole frame.
tune.go: Find the settings closest to the picture
tune.hint: Tries a few dozen settings of the sliders under Adjust the picture and of Emphasise outlines and Emphasise dark detail, works out the winding for each, and keeps the one whose piece looks most like the picture. Invert, the brush and the thread colours stay as they are. It takes ten seconds to a minute.
tune.changed: Adjusted: similarity to the picture {before}% → {after}%. Press Generate to see the result.
tune.kept: Nothing tried looks more like the picture than the current settings (similarity {percent}%).
tune.note: These settings were found automatically: similarity to the picture {before}% → {after}%.
tune.moved: The settings were changed while it was working, so what it found was not applied. Press it again.
tune.blank: {percent}% of this picture is as light as the board, like a line drawing. That is the hardest kind of picture for string art: every line crosses the whole frame, so the lines that draw an outline also grey the empty parts. Besides the automatic adjustment, a white thread wound last helps a great deal: it covers the black lines where the picture is empty, at about five times the lines.
tune.blankInside: {percent}% of this picture is as light as the board, like a line drawing. With pins inside the picture a line can run along a stroke. A white thread wound last makes the piece more like the picture still: it covers the black lines where the picture is empty. On eight test drawings the similarity rose from 68 % to 83 %, at about four times the lines.
tune.addWhite: Switch to black, then white, on a white board
tune.insideNote: For a line drawing there is another way: pins inside the picture, so that lines can run along its strokes. On eight test drawings the similarity rose from 56 % to 68 % with a black thread, and to 83 % with a white one as well, at the price of a few hundred more pins and about twice the lines.
importance.hint: Lines crowd near the rim, so backgrounds there look busy. Quiet rim lets the centre win a little. Centre first counts the outer part for a tenth; Centre only does not count it at all: it will be a tangle, and in return the centre comes closer to the picture with far fewer lines. The similarity number and the automatic adjustment then judge only what counts. The blue veil on the picture is the part that counts for less, and the brush can make any place count again.
importance.edgesHint: Where lightness changes sharply (outlines, the edges of features) counts for more than flat areas.
importance.toneHint: Dark parts get darker and the contrast grows; in return light parts turn greyer and more thread is used.
gen.resHint: Pixels across the frame while computing. Higher is finer and slower.
gen.minSkipHint: Fewest pins between two consecutive pins; avoids short lines along the rim.
gen.repeat: Allow the same pin pair again (up to 3 times)
gen.repeatHint: Lets lines stack where the picture is very dark. When off, a thread runs between the same two pins only once.
gen.repeatInside: Does not apply with pins inside the picture: a thread draws a pair of pins once, and runs between them again only to get somewhere else.
gen.alpha: One line covers {alpha} of a pixel it crosses (keep it at 0.5 or below).
issue.alpha: The thread is too thick for that resolution, so the resolution was lowered.
issue.min-skip: The minimum skip was lowered to the most this frame allows: a round frame needs at least twice the skip plus one pins, and on a rectangular frame the skip is at most a quarter of the pins.
issue.frame: A frame value was out of range and was corrected.
issue.thread: The thread width was out of range and was corrected.
issue.generator: The resolution was out of range and was corrected.
issue.budget: A line budget was out of range and was corrected.
issue.thread-equals-board: The first thread has the board's colour, so its lines will not show. Wind it later, or change a colour.
issue.duplicate-thread: Two threads have the same colour.
issue.thread-colour: A thread colour was not a valid colour and was replaced.
issue.threads-count: Only the first six threads were kept.
issue.board-colour: The board colour was not a valid colour and was replaced.
issue.frame-shape: The shape of the frame in this file is not one this page knows; it was read as a circle.
issue.crop: The crop was out of range and was corrected.
issue.adjust: An adjustment was out of range and was corrected.
issue.image: The picture's size in the file was not valid.
issue.importance: Some brush strokes in the file were not valid and were left out.
issue.player: The player's settings were out of range and were corrected.
issue.project-version: This project was saved by a different version; it was read as well as possible.
issue.result: The winding sequence in the file does not fit its settings and was left out.
issue.brush-png: The file's painted importance map is in a format this version does not read; it was left out.
run.empty: No line would bring the board closer to this picture: it is already as light as the board. Darken the picture, or choose other colours.
run.stopped: Stopped early. What is there can be used, or continued.
run.budget: The line budget ran out while lines would still help ({names}). Raise the budget, or lower the darkness.
run.unstarted: No line of {names} would help, so none was wound.
result.stale: The settings have changed since this result was generated.

stage.targetHint: This is the picture the lines will try to match, inside the frame of pins.
stage.cropHint: Drag to move the picture, scroll or pinch to zoom. The arrow keys, + and - work too.
stage.brushHint: Paint where the picture matters more (orange) or less (blue).
stage.gamutHint: Hatched: colours these threads cannot mix.
stage.modelHint: The quick preview: how dense the lines are in each spot.
stage.realisticHint: Every line drawn at its true width, in winding order.
stage.sideHint: The picture on the left, the result on the right.
stage.wipeHint: Drag the divider: the picture is on its left, the result on its right.
